story_candidates.title: What '99.9% uptime' covers: how AI and cloud providers count downtime

ai_path.connection: Direct: how AI providers promise reliability.

story_candidates.angle: An explainer on what an uptime promise covers, read from five providers' own pages and not ranked.
story_candidates.note: For journalist-ai, category AI. Ready (Vicky's word of 26 Nov about 12:40 UTC, passed on by the conductor's task 2026-11-26-1250-curator-uptime-explainer; this lifts the 'research only' hold of task 2026-11-26-1100-curator-hold-uptime for this explainer only). Angle: what a '99.9% uptime' promise actually covers. The percentage is common, but what counts as 'down', over what period and whether partial problems count differ by provider; a reader choosing tools, AI tools included, should read how downtime is counted, not only the number. Rests only on the six captures (Google's Gemini API SLA, OpenAI's Scale Tier page, Anthropic's service tiers page and Commercial Terms, GitLab's availability handbook page, AWS's EC2 SLA page) and NOT on the GitHub incident captures or any GitHub figure or anything about 25 November. Read each page yourself. Attribute each provider's terms to its own page with the date read; where a page does not define downtime, the period or credits, say so (the OpenAI and Anthropic captures list these as unknown); OpenAI's 99.9% is for Scale Tier (Enterprise customers) and Anthropic's 99.5% target is for the Priority Tier (organizations with a capacity commitment), not for all use; Anthropic's Commercial Terms say services are provided 'AS IS' and 'AS AVAILABLE' and do not warrant uninterrupted use, and no uptime commitment appears in the captured quotes; Google's definition (a more than five percent error rate for five or more consecutive minutes, per calendar month, credits as the sole remedy) is the one page that defines downtime precisely, so set the others beside it without ranking providers. You may include the simple arithmetic of what a percentage allows over a month (99.9% is about 43 minutes, 99.5% about 3.6 hours, 99.99% about 4 minutes), stated as arithmetic and not as a provider's figure. No claim beyond what the pages say. The AI connection is direct (how AI providers promise reliability) and goes in the data note. Explain 'uptime', 'SLA' and 'service credit' in plain words at first use; 400 to 800 words.

for_the_fact_checker.what: Each provider's terms are its own page as captured (dates read 26 Nov 12:07 to 12:40 UTC); OpenAI and Anthropic pages leave downtime, period and credits unstated in the captured quotes; the arithmetic is the writer's and should be checked.
